soundness_flags.label: def:observed-adaptive-law / def:exact-b-designs
soundness_flags.one_line: q is typed as an integer vector yet is used as a history-indexed map q_b(h), while its F_{b-1}-measurability is stated relative to the very law being constructed; define deterministic measurable policy maps on canonical prefix-history spaces before invoking the kernels.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper derives an average-propensity semiparametric lower bound and implementable batched designs approaching that benchmark, including a sharp second-order rate for linear outcome-mean functionals.

source_verification_receipts.locator: §4, Theorem 4.1 and discussion; §5, Theorem 5.1 and Algorithm 2
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper analyzes two-stage and multistage adaptive Neyman allocation through competitive ratios using earlier-stage variance estimates.
The paper proposes a two-wave conditional-minimax-regret allocation rule based on finite-sample variance confidence sets and states minimax-regret attainment up to constants.
The paper fixes the total number of batches and lets each batch size diverge when developing Batched OLS inference.
The paper develops limiting data environments for sequential decisions with endogenous information sets and illustrates batched adaptive experiments.
The paper derives first-order efficiency bounds for adaptive assignments based on covariates and past outcomes.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace q with a sequence of explicit Borel maps from canonical prefix histories to feasible integer counts, then define the filtration and chronological law from those maps; restate all predictability claims against that canonical construction.

Make the flagship comparison more auditable by adding a short theorem-level table separating the exact-B MSE game from Li--Simchi-Levi, Zhao, and Yamin along loss, design class, count constraint, and lower-bound scope.

Strengthen the eventual headline with an explicit finite worked schedule at a small nontrivial (n,B), including its exact counts, weights, risk, and lattice loss, to make the constructive optimal-design certificate concrete.

recommended_next_step: Repair the policy-space/law-construction circularity, then advance the every-B frontier angle to Stage 0; its central novelty survives both repo and published comparison.
